title: Release readiness thermometer and signal slate — Nov 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight preflight "thermometer" and signal catalog for the upcoming rollout (internal feature toggle: routing-v2). Use this doc as the single source for: release-day checks, signal thresholds, quick mitigation steps, and a terse release-notes draft to cut into the customer-facing one-pager.

High-level summary (one line):
- Gradual traffic migration to routing-v2 with region-aware fallback and a DSTable KV-cache change. Primary risk: latency regressions on long-sequence chat flows.

Readiness thermometer (current snapshot, updated by owners):
- Infra (capacity + autoscale config): 85% — reserved capacity validated in us-west-2, burst behavior needs one more smoke run (Diego).
- Serving runtime (kernel selection knobs): 70% — integration tests passed; long-seq perf still 10–15% behind baseline on RTX-80XX emulation (Priya).
- Telemetry & alerts: 80% — dashboards created, alerts drafted; sampling filters for trace capture outstanding (Liam).
- Canary tests / e2e: 60% — chat regression harness flaky under concurrent load, need additional stability run.
- Docs & runbooks: 90% — release notes and quick rollback steps drafted but comm templates need sign-off.
- Overall go/no-go score: 77% (alpha threshold for soft-launch = 80%)

Short calendar (week leading to release):
- D-7 (2026-11-18): Final smoke with reserved infra + kernel candidate A. Owners: Diego/Priya.
- D-5 (2026-11-20): Telemetry validation — ensure span sampling and token-level cost metrics show up in dashboards (Liam).
- D-3 (2026-11-22): Canary config bake (1% traffic), create watchlist and opt-in cohort.
- D-1 (2026-11-24): Go/No-go review meeting 10:00 PT. Ops desk + SRE + product.
- Release day (2026-11-25): Staggered ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation per step.

Release-day hour-by-hour cadence (compact):
- T+00:00: Preflight checks (ticket open, comm channels in Slack, stage gating in CI green).
- T+00:15: Route small internal test cohort (non-customer) through routing-v2. Verify 95th perc latency < baseline * 1.6.
- T+00:45: Lift to 1% production; run regression prompts set A through the traffic router.
- T+01:15: If no alerts, 5% traffic. If latency drift > 1.4x baseline for 5 minutes, HOLD and run rollback.
- T+X: Continue ramps with 30 minute dwell and manual signoff at 5% and 20%.

Signal catalog (what to watch and thresholds):
- latency_p95_overall: threshold = baseline_p95 * 1.4 sustained for 5m -> page SRE primary.
- kv_cache_miss_ratio: threshold = >8% sustained -> investigate DS table miss pattern (Potential model warming issue).
- token_cost_per_call: threshold = >1.25x expected median -> spike may indicate runaway generation loops.
- error_rate_5m: >0.5% -> page ENG-ops and slow traffic.
- model_fallback_rate: any non-zero fallback for >2% of requests in 10m -> rollback candidate; likely indicates incompatible tokenizer/quantization mismatch.
- reroute_success_ratio: <99% on fallback path -> escalate to routing-owner.

Playbook: quick mitigation steps (ordered):
1) Throttle traffic to safety lane (move to dedicated capacity tier B).
2) Disable KV-cache prefixing change (feature flag: kv-prefix-v2 = OFF).
3) Pin model variant to legacy quantization (variant: v1-quant) for affected route.
4) Revert routing policy for a region (region flag: route-v2-asia = OFF).
5) If rollback needed, follow "atomic rollback" procedure in Confluence-RELEASE-214 and notify customers as per comm template.

Ownership matrix (single-line entries):
- Release lead: Ava Chen (overall decisions, go/no-go).
- Infra/Capacity: Diego Martinez (capacity, autoscale).
- Serving runtime: Priya Singh (kernel knobs, perf).
- Telemetry & Alerts: Liam O'Connor (dashboards, thresholds).
- QA/Canary: Maya Patel (harness, regression sets).
- Communications: Rajesh Kumar (status page, release notes).

Release notes draft (skeleton — publishable after edits):
- Title: Progressive rollout: routing-v2 (KV-cache improvements)
- Short summary: We are rolling out routing-v2 which improves prefix-aware KV cache utilization and reduces cold-start token cost for multi-turn chats. The rollout will be gradual and region-aware with automatic fallbacks to routing-v1.
- Impact: Improved per-token cost for long chat sessions; possible brief latency variability during early ramps. No change to API surface or client SDKs.
- Rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over ~4–6 hours with manual checks at 5% and 20%.
- How to opt-out: Customers with strict latency SLAs can contact support to remain on routing-v1 for 24–72 hours.
- Known limitations: Some long-sequence edge prompts may see slightly higher latency until warmup completes; token-cost measurement is still being tuned.
- Contact & postmortem: eng-release@redwood.com. Post-release telemetry review and short-form postmortem scheduled D+2.

Unresolved questions / notes to investigate (notes-to-self style):
- Canary harness: why does the concurrent-run failure correlate with GPU memory transient OOMs on emulation? (Potential memory fragmentation in the kernel selector path).
- Trace sampling: switch to deterministic sampling for the rollout cohort to avoid missing pre/post-fault spans. Confirm cost impact.
- Fallback hysteresis: current routing fallback flips after 2 consecutive failures — should we increase to 3 for noisy signals?

Preflight checklist (tick boxes for the D-1 runbook):
- [ ] CI green for all model variants + integration smoke
- [ ] Reserve infra capacity tested at 1.5x expected peak
- [ ] Canary harness run X3 with stable outputs
- [ ] Dashboards show token cost, p95 latency, kv-miss ratio, fallback rate
- [ ] Pager rules tested in staging and notifications validated
- [ ] Comms templates in #release-ops prepared
- [ ] On-call and escalation rotation confirmed for release window

Post-release quick audit (D+0, D+1):
- D+0: verify reroute_success_ratio and kv_cache_miss_ratio back to baseline within 4h of full ramp.
- D+1: run the full regression set B over live traffic snapshot and compare generation quality metrics (BLEU-style / embedding drift sampling).
- D+2: convene 45m postmortem; if any regression > 5% in quality or >20% cost delta, trigger rollback decision tree.

Notes/links: (copy-paste in meeting)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-214 (rollout runbook)
- Jira epic: JIRA-REL-5678
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tooling/pull/423

Quick sign-off checklist (for the Go/No-go meeting):
- Infra signed off (Diego)
- Serving perf acceptance (Priya)
- Telemetry validation (Liam)
- QA flakiness resolve or approved risk (Maya)
- Product aware of customer-facing notes (Rajesh)

TODOs (who-does-what before D-3):
- Priya: run long-seq perf with kernel-candidate-B and upload results to artifact bucket (due D-6).
- Diego: run one more reserved-capacity burst test with synthetic traffic (due D-7).
- Liam: finalize alert sampling filters and push alert definitions to production (due D-5).
- Maya: stabilize canary harness concurrency envelope (due D-4).

Last comment: this is intentionally terse — use it during the go/no-go huddle and paste the release-notes skeleton into the customer-facing doc after Go.

-- Ava
